1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 3: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 58:  p300.aspirate(23.0, master_mix_pool)
   At line 58 the p300_single_gen2 draws 23 ul from well A1 in slot 3 with its tip 1 mm
   above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 189 ul, which in this NEST 12 Well
   Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.88 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this
   line did it 7 times, after 4 times in the liquid; 161 ul of air in all). The simulator
   does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 7 wells filled from these draws got
   air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 3.
   Also reached 7 other wells: wells A6, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11 and A12 in slot 2.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html

   line 62:  p20.aspirate(2, block[sample_well_names[i]])

   the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 in slot 2.

1 more went in (8% of the well)

   well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small
   well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you
   calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one

findings.title: A temperature module was loaded but never set
findings.explanation: At line 41 the robot draws from wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 9 more in slot 1, on a temperature module that the protocol never sets. A temperature module stays at room temperature until `set_temperature` is called, so buffer (carrier), fwd primer (reagent), polymerase (reagent), rev primer (reagent) and 13 more sat on a block that was never cold; the robot pipetted there 17 times over the run. The person setting up the deck sees a module and assumes it is cold. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 9 more in slot 1.
findings.fix: Call `temp_module.set_temperature(4)` before the first transfer from Opentrons 24 Well Aluminum Block with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap in slot 1, and `temp_module.deactivate()` at the end.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: fwd primer (well A3 in slot 1)
findings.explanation: At line 48 the tip went into fwd primer (well A3 in slot 1) while it still carried buffer (well A1 in slot 1), polymerase (well A2 in slot 1) and water (well A5 in slot 1) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted material along into 7 other wells: wells A6, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11 and A12 in slot 2.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 48 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.explanation: At line 50 the tip went into rev primer (well A4 in slot 1) while it still carried buffer (well A1 in slot 1), polymerase (well A2 in slot 1), fwd primer (well A3 in slot 1) and water (well A5 in slot 1) from an earlier step. findings.title: Liquid drawn from well A1 in slot 3 before it was mixed: added at line 51, drawn at line 53 and line 58
findings.explanation: At line 51 liquid was added to well A1 in slot 3, which already held a different liquid. At line 53 and line 58 liquid was drawn out of it again, and the well was never mixed in between. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the tip drew is not at the concentration you calculated. In a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
findings.fix: Mix the well after the addition at line 51: `mix_after=(5, volume)` in a transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, volume, well)`. Integra suggests about 5 cycles at about 80% of the volume in the well.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: water (well A5 in slot 1)
findings.explanation: At line 43 the tip went into water (well A5 in slot 1) while it still carried buffer (well A1 in slot 1) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from it again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 43 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: No no-template control: 5 wells of polymerase with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 56 the robot starts putting polymerase into Bio-Rad 96 Well Plate 200 µL PCR (slot 2), and 5 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 in slot 2.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 0.5 ul of polymerase and 2 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: 5 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 1 more went in (8% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 63 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 1 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 in slot 2, which already held buffer, water, polymerase, fwd primer and 1 more (this line did it 5 times). The addition was 8% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5 in slot 2 after line 63: `mix_after=(5, 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
